subject: Renewal proposal: Harmonize term + conditional burst buckets
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: Harmonize term + conditional burst buckets

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the thoughtful conversation last week. Per our call I attached a concise renewal proposal (RDW-Acme_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf) that aims to accomplish three things: 1) align your Redwood contract with your fiscal year (Jan start), 2) simplify billing by harmonizing to a 24-month term with an annualized commit ladder, and 3) add a conditional burst/fallback bucket for unexpected spikes while protecting unit economics for Acme.

Top-line from the attachment: a 24-month term with an annualized commit of 45% in year one and 55% in year two (we call this a front-loaded onramp), plus a capped burst bucket at 20% of committed QPS that can be used at a higher overage rate if consumption exceeds committed run-rate. We included two concession options: a 7% committed discount for the 24-month commitment or a 10% discount if you prepay year one in full.

I know procurement will have questions about auto-renew and proration — we left both as configurable: auto-renew default is off, and pro rata run-in/out rules are in section 4. 

Next steps proposed:
- You: confirm if Acme prefers auto-renew ON or OFF and whether prepay is an option
- Us: once you confirm, we can produce a tracked SOW for signatures and lock in the committed pricing.xlsx numbers

I copied Kimberly (Pricing) and Priyom (CS ops) for technical/billing questions. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk the doc.

Best,
Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-Acme_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal summary), committed-pricing-breakdown.xlsx (line-item pricing)

Diego —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and clear doc. A few clarifying questions from procurement:
1) How would proration work if our fiscal year change means a mid-quarter start? (we need clear run-in and run-out numbers)
2) Can the burst bucket be auto-top-up or is it strictly post-usage invoiced? If auto-top-up, we need a hard cap per month.
3) Auto-renew: team prefers OFF by default but we'd consider ON if there's a 90-day price-notice clause and an escape clause on material changes.

Separately, are you able to provide an example invoice flow showing a quarter where we consume 130% of committed (100% committed + 30% burst)? Procurement also requested a short summary of legal-friendly language for the term and termination sections to feed to our counsel.

Can we schedule 11/2 or 11/4 for a 30-min walkthrough?

—Sara

Subject: RE: Renewal proposal: Harmonize term + conditional burst buckets

Diego / Priyom —

Notes for call and options to present to Acme:
- Proration: propose calendar-day proration with a 30-day run-in window and pro-rata credits for early termination (standard language). If they move start to mid-quarter, invoice will show a pro-rated first invoice and a straight monthly cadence afterwards.
- Burst handling: two operational options we can offer:
  a) Post-usage invoicing (default) — burst billed monthly at "burst rate" = committed unit price * 1.8 (example in attachment).
  b) Auto-top-up with hard cap (customer-controlled) — we can top-up from a prepaid escrow balance that we draw against; unused escrow returns at renewal. This adds two admin items but meets procurement's cap request.
- Auto-renew: toggle OFF by default. If they want ON, require 90-day notice + price-notice clause and maintain a unilateral 30-day mutual termination window for material changes.

Pricing note: if they choose auto-top-up escrow we recommend a smaller discount (5%) vs the 7% committed-only discount. Prepay gives the deeper 10% as Diego proposed.

I'll join the call to run the pricing sheet. Priyom, can you prepare an example invoice scenario (130% consumption) for tomorrow?

—Kimberly
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Renewal proposal: Harmonize term + conditional burst buckets

Hi Sara / team —

Appended the invoice example inline to make the math explicit:

Scenario: Quarterly committed spend (Q) = $100,000
- Committed usage covered: $100,000
- Burst usage (30% overage) = $30,000 equivalent tokens
- Burst billing option A (post-usage): burst rate = 1.8x committed unit price => burst invoice = $54,000
  => Total invoice = $154,000 for that quarter
- If they prepay Year 1 and take the 10% prepay discount, committed portion reduces to $90,000 (example), burst still billed at 1.8x unless otherwise negotiated.

Operational notes:
- Auto-top-up escrow flow: we would hold a prepaid pool (e.g., $50k) that draws down; monthly reconciliation shows draw, and we send a statement. If the escrow hits the hard cap, we stop auto-top-up and notify procurement.
- Proration example: if start date is Nov 10 and their fiscal quarter begins Nov 1, first invoice will show 21/90 days prorated amount = 23.3% of the quarter's committed charge (line item shown in attached committed-pricing-breakdown.xlsx).

Sara — if those numbers look reasonable, Diego and I can produce a short legal-friendly term snippet for the contract team and build the DocuSign package for a signature path (optionally separate SOW for prepay).

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
